inputs.share_count_basis: 4,586.18m shares in issue at 2026-06-30 less 63.00m treasury shares = 4,523.18m, plus 52.95m unvested share awards (2024 Share Award Scheme) and 1.35m vested Pre-IPO options = 4,577.5m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The US$250m Alibaba convertible bond (327.4m shares at HK$6.00) is EXCLUDED from the count and carried as debt at principal: it is 40% out of the money at the current price. If the bull case plays out above HK$6.00 it converts, adding 327m shares against RMB~1,700m of debt extinguished -- roughly 3% dilutive to the bull value, not modelled.
inputs.cash_basis: Company's own 'cash and other liquid financial resources' at 2026-06-30: cash and cash equivalents 1,359.98 + term deposits 2,287.32 current and 695.01 non-current + short-term investments 442.00 + long-term treasury investments 34.57 = 4,818.88. Restricted cash 1.9 excluded. Term deposits and treasury investments are bank deposits / bank wealth-management products redeemable at or before maturity -- they are the cash pile after the H1 2026 reallocation out of cash equivalents (cash fell 3,514 -> 1,360 while deposits rose 498 -> 2,982).
inputs.debt_basis: Bank borrowings 60.0 (1.75%, current) + Alibaba convertible bond at PRINCIPAL ~RMB1,700 (US$250m at ~6.8 USDCNY end-June 2026; 1% coupon, matures 2028-12-31). The balance-sheet carrying value is the fair-valued debt component 1,422.2; principal is what is repaid if not converted, so principal is the conservative claim. The RMB187.0m subsidiary convertible redeemable preferred shares were redeemed in H1 2026 (184.1 paid) and are nil. Lease liabilities (40.7) excluded -- leases are charged inside EBIT (treatment B).
inputs.sbc_source: TTM Jun-2026: FY2025 share-based compensation 118.496 (AR FY2025 cash-flow note, line 13571) + H1 2026 65.566 - H1 2025 57.421 (interim adjusted-net-profit reconciliation, line 875). No net-share-settlement taxes are disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). The FY2025 RMB511.8m 'share-based non-cash expense from convertible bonds issuance' is NOT SBC: it is the day-one fair value of the Alibaba CB above principal, a one-off financing charge, and is excluded from the SBC series (kept as the ConvertibleBondNonCashExpense KPI). NOTE: the Metrics.csv carries H1 FY2026 SBC = 30.165 and H1 FY2025 = 25.089, which do not match the filings' 65.566 / 57.421 reconciliation lines -- flagged for the parser.
inputs.interest_income_basis: Only the interest received INSIDE operating cash flow is stripped (FY2025 2.410 + H1 2026 3.408 - H1 2025 2.531 = 3.3). Investment income on term deposits and treasury investments (59.1 in H1 2026, 47.3 in H1 2025) is classified in INVESTING activities and is therefore already outside reported FCF; the P&L finance-income line (55-73/yr) is not in the flows. Net cash of ~3,059 is 2.6x the FCF base, so the rule applies.
inputs.buyback_note: H1 2026 payments for shares repurchase RMB240.3m (63.0m shares now held in treasury); nil FY2020-FY2025. Dividends: HK$0.05 final (RMB197.6m paid Jun-2026) + HK$0.067 interim declared. The flat count is being funded for the first time.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1727, Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T09:55Z. Cross-check: USDHKD 7.8474 / USDCNY 6.6756 = 1.1755 (0.2% tie). Direction/parity check from the filing: FY2025 final dividend HK$227.4m paid as RMB197.7m in June 2026 = 1.150 CNY->HKD, consistent with CNY strengthening since. Per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by fx_rate to HKD; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in HKD, comparable to current_price.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the twelve months to 2026-06-30 (FY2025 + H1 2026 - H1 2025), so the flows start from the same date as the balance sheet and the H1 2026 cash generation is not counted both in net cash and in year 1. Year 1 = Jul-2026..Jun-2027. TTM revenue 3,858.7 + 2,212.8 - 1,812.9 = 4,258.6; OCF 1,257.0 + 605.5 - 503.6 = 1,358.9; capex 46.9 + 18.3 - 30.2 = 35.0; reported FCF 1,323.9.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% risk-free, China equity risk premium ~6.5%, beta ~1.25 for a HK-listed small/mid-cap Chinese consumer-software name -> cost of equity ~9.9%, rounded to 10.0%. Net cash and a 1% coupon CB mean debt has no weight. The same 10.0% is used in all three scenarios: AI-commoditisation, China-consumer and regulatory risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the rate (charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. The lease charge (FY2025 payments for lease liabilities 34.6 + interest ~0.3 = 0.9% of revenue; H1 2026 14.2 = 0.64%) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, lease liabilities (40.7 at 2026-06-30) are EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: PPE 35.7 + intangibles 15.7 = 51.4 = 1.33% of revenue; ROU depreciation 32.5 excluded) so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are a NEGATIVE RMB37.0m (loss-making minority stakes in subsidiaries; NCI share of profit -2.0m in H1 2026, -35.5m FY2025 mostly from the discontinued beauty-solutions business). Immaterial and adverse to the NCI, so no bridge deduction; flows are treated as 100% attributable.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Adjusted EBITDA = gross profit - S&M - admin - R&D - net impairment on financial assets + other income, EXCLUDING other gains/losses (fair-value changes on investments, crypto disposal gains), the CB day-one charge, intangible impairments, finance income and associates; then + SBC + D&A ex-ROU. FY2025: 850.8 + 118.5 + 51.4 = 1,020.7 = 26.5%; H1 2025 27.7%; H1 2026 29.6%; TTM ~27.6%. Pre-SBC and post-lease, so sbc_pct_path and lease_cost_pct_path are both deducted from it.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: subscription photo/video/design software, 77% of revenue, plus advertising 20%). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (non-US operating company) with the adaptations file applied: CNY flows vs HKD quote (fx_rate bridge), leases treatment B, NCI immaterial, matching-asset rule for the long-term investment portfolio (see equity_bridge). First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF. The qualitative Analysis.json was not yet present when this was built -- the scenario axes are drawn from the H1 2026 interim report and FY2025 annual report directly. Cash tax: TTM cash taxes paid were only 58.7 (5.5% of EBIT) thanks to HNTE 15% / software-enterprise 10% preferential rates and brought-forward losses; the FY2025 P&L charge of 207.9 is mostly deferred tax on investment fair-value gains and is not a cash cost. The path ramps toward ~17% (15% HNTE plus withholding on repatriation). Working capital: contract liabilities (deferred subscription revenue) rose 182.5 over the TTM on revenue growth of 1,070.7, a 17% capture, modelled at 15% on the CHANGE in revenue. Gross margin fell 75.3% -> 71.5% in H1 2026 on AI inference/API cost in the early-stage productivity apps; the base margin path lets operating leverage offset that only slowly.

equity_bridge.item: Long-term investment portfolio (associates/JVs 1,142.2 + FVTPL 1,072.3 + FVOCI 15.9 = 2,230.4) net of deferred tax liabilities 369.7, at a 25% illiquidity haircut
equity_bridge.note: Interim 2026-06-30 balance sheet. Matching-asset rule: fair-value gains, share of associates' results and the 13.3 dividend income from investees are all outside owner FCF, so the assets enter the bridge. Mostly private AI/tech stakes (e.g. ~1.3% of Enflame, which listed on the STAR Board on 2026-09-11 -- not re-marked here). The haircut and the DTL deduction are conservative; the FY2025 FVTPL gain of 517.3 and H1 2026 gain of 237.8 show the carrying values move a lot.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: H1 FY2026 run-rate (+22.1% YoY, subscribers +19.7%) tempered for tougher H2 comps (H2 2025 +48.8%) and a declining advertising line; equity 3yr CAGR of 15.0% is the floor the path decelerates through
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 15.0% vs revenue 3yr CAGR 22.8% (34% divergence) and EPS 3yr CAGR 81.7% off a near-zero FY2022 base. Equity is depressed by RMB865.6m of FY2025 dividends and the H1 2026 buyback, not by weak earnings; revenue is the better guide. Base path starts at 18% and decelerates to 3.5% by year 10.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue is on the restated continuing-operations basis (crypto and the divested beauty-solutions business excluded). Owner FCF: FY2022 183.6 - 47.3 SBC - ~3 interest = 133.3 -> FY2025 1,089.2 (3yr CAGR 101%), versus reported FCF 87.6% -- SBC was a larger share of cash flow in the base year, so the owner series grew faster, the opposite of the usual warning. FY2020 owner FCF was negative (-309), so 5yr FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined. FY2023-24 reported FCF excludes the crypto disposal proceeds (investing activities).

base.narrative: Subscription growth continues at a decelerating pace: overseas paying subscribers (higher ARPPU) and the productivity apps (ARR RMB620m, Kaipai/Vmake doubling-tripling) carry growth while advertising keeps shrinking low-single digits and leisure-app MAU is flat. Gross margin stabilises near 71-72% as inference cost per unit falls; opex grows slower than gross profit, lifting the pre-SBC EBITDA margin from ~28% to 31%. Cash tax ramps from the current 8% toward 17% as preferential rates and loss carry-forwards wind down. Terminal 3% CNY nominal growth, capped at 15x year-10 owner FCF.

bull.narrative: Globalisation and the productivity pivot both work: overseas subscribers in East Asia, Latin America and Europe keep compounding at high ARPPU, the subscription rate climbs from 6.5% toward 9-10% of a stable 280m MAU, and usage-based AI-credit consumption (growing 46% QoQ in H1 2026) removes the fixed spend ceiling of subscription tiers. Self-developed models (96% of outputs) keep third-party API cost at mid-single digits so gross margin recovers toward 74-75% and the EBITDA margin reaches 37% on operating leverage. The Alibaba e-commerce partnership scales Kaipai/MVLAND into merchant workflows. Note the CB would convert above HK$6.00 in this scenario (~3% dilution not modelled).

bear.narrative: Frontier image/video models from Google, ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent are bundled free into phones, chat assistants and e-commerce platforms, commoditising the editing layer that Meitu and BeautyCam sell; leisure-app MAU (already -3% YoY) erodes and churn rises, so paying subscribers plateau in 2027 and decline from 2028. Advertising keeps falling. Inference and API costs do not fall as fast as pricing, gross margin slides toward the mid-60s, and R&D must be held to defend the model stack, compressing the EBITDA margin to 18%. The productivity apps grow but are too small (ARR 620m) to offset the core. The CB stays out of the money and is repaid in cash in Dec-2028 from the cash pile.

scenario_narratives.base: Subscription growth decelerates from ~20% to mid-single digits over a decade as overseas and productivity apps offset flat leisure MAU and a shrinking ad line; EBITDA margin drifts up 3pts on operating leverage; cash tax normalises toward 17%; 15x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Globalisation plus usage-based AI credits lift the subscription rate toward 9-10% and ARPPU higher; self-developed models hold gross margin; EBITDA margin reaches 37%; 18x terminal cap. CB conversion dilution (~3%) not modelled.
scenario_narratives.bear: Free frontier image models commoditise photo editing; subscribers peak in 2027, revenue falls ~15% peak-to-trough, EBITDA margin compresses to 18%; 12x terminal cap; CB repaid in cash.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (AI productivity apps are ~15% of revenue) while the core leisure product faces a structural free-model threat, and the share price has fallen 62% from its 52-week high, which says the market is actively pricing that outcome. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right -- overseas subscriber compounding, the subscription-rate step-up and gross-margin recovery against inference costs. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Meitu is valued as an owner-FCF stream from a subscription software business with ~RMB3.1bn of net cash and a RMB1.4bn investment portfolio behind it. The flows are built from components -- pre-SBC EBITDA margin, SBC at ~3% of revenue (expensed, count held flat), lease cost inside EBIT, D&A ex-ROU, a cash-tax ramp from 8% to 17%, and deferred-revenue capture on the change in revenue -- rather than carrying the TTM 28% owner-FCF margin forward, because the TTM figure embeds a 5.5% cash tax rate and a working-capital tailwind that both fade. Value is computed in CNY and converted to HKD at the dated rate. The dominant uncertainty is not the discount rate but whether frontier generative-image models absorb the casual editing use case; that risk lives in the bear path and a 25% bear weight, not in a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: Generative-AI commoditisation of photo/video editing by platform-bundled frontier models (Google, ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent) -- the bear axis; leisure-app MAU already -3% YoY.
Gross-margin compression from inference/API cost in early-stage productivity apps (71.5% in H1 2026 vs 75.3%); the base assumes it stabilises.
Advertising (20% of revenue) in structural decline (-4.4% H1 2026, -1.3% FY2025).
App-store take rates (revenue sharing fee to Apple/Google is the largest cost of sales, 375.6 in H1 2026).
Cash tax normalisation: TTM cash tax was 5.5% of EBIT; the path ramps to 17% but the timing of preferential-rate expiry and loss utilisation is uncertain either way.
Alibaba convertible bond: RMB~1,700m principal due Dec-2028 carried as debt; converts at HK$6.00 (327m shares, ~7% dilution) only in a bull outcome.
Investment portfolio in the bridge (RMB1,395m after haircut) is mostly private stakes marked to fair value; carrying values swung +517 in FY2025.
China regulatory and MIIT approval uncertainty (interim report risk section), and CNY/HKD translation of the per-share value.
